file: Luther at the Diet of Worms.jpg

caption: The Joseph Smith birthplace memorial at Sharon, Vermont, with the granite obelisk dedicated in December 1905, as published in 1907.
credit: Photographer unknown; published in the Improvement Era, December 1907

caption: The grove west of the Smith farm in Manchester, New York, known to Latter-day Saints as the Sacred Grove, photographed about 1907.
credit: George Edward Anderson (1860–1928), photograph, about 1907

caption: The hill about three miles from the Smith farm, now called the Hill Cumorah, photographed in 1907.
credit: George Edward Anderson (1860–1928), photograph, 1907

file: Joseph Smith family farm in Manchester.jpg
caption: The Smith family farm in Manchester, New York, the land Alvin worked to pay for, photographed about 1907.
credit: George Edward Anderson (1860–1928), photograph, about 1907

caption: The angel Moroni and Joseph Smith at the hill, as C.C.A. Christensen painted the scene in the nineteenth century.

caption: November 1833: Latter-day Saints driven from Jackson County, Missouri, in Christensen's painting.

after: Joseph never spoke publicly about this vision
caption: The Melchizedek Priesthood pulpits at the west end of the Kirtland Temple's lower hall, photographed in 1912, with a curtain rolled up overhead. It was behind curtains at these upper pulpits that Joseph and Oliver knelt on April 3, 1836.
credit: C. Edward Miller, photograph, copyrighted 1912; Library of Congress

caption: Nauvoo about 1846, with the temple on the bluff in the distance. One of the earliest photographs of the city.
credit: Lucien R. Foster, daguerreotype, about 1846

caption: The Nauvoo Temple on the bluff above the city, as Christensen painted it.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), The Nauvoo Temple, 19th century

file: Joseph Mustering the Nauvoo Legion by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: Joseph Smith with the Nauvoo Legion, in Christensen's painting.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Joseph Mustering the Nauvoo Legion, 19th century

file: Exterior of Carthage Jail by C.C.A. Christensen.png
caption: Carthage Jail, June 27, 1844, as Christensen painted it decades later, with a shaft of light at the window where Joseph fell.
credit: C.C.A. Christensen (1831–1912), Exterior of Carthage Jail, 19th century

credit: Louis R. Chaffin (attributed), daguerreotype, about 1847

file: William Tyndale translating the Bible into English.png
caption: William Tyndale at work on his translation, as a Victorian illustrator imagined him. No portrait made from life survives.
credit: Alexander Johnston, illustration in The Church of England: A History for the People, 1898

caption: Tyndale's execution at Vilvoorde, from the woodcut in John Foxe's Actes and Monuments (the Book of Martyrs).

file: Moritz Daniel Oppenheim - Seder (The Passover Meal) (Der Oster-Abend) - Google Art Project.jpg

caption: A New England farm in a lithograph of 1853. It is not the Smith farm. It shows the kind of hill-country farming the family took up in Tunbridge.
credit: Fanny Palmer (1812–1876), artist; N. Currier, publisher, American Farm Scenes No. 1, lithograph, 1853; Library of Congress

caption: Title page of Lucy Mack Smith's history of her family (Liverpool, 1853), the main source for this chapter.
credit: Lucy Smith, Biographical Sketches of Joseph Smith the Prophet, and His Progenitors for Many Generations, 1853

sec: "As Sure As There Is a God in Heaven"
caption: A New England homestead in winter, from an 1868 lithograph. The Smiths set out over roads like these in the winter of 1816–17.
credit: Currier & Ives, American Homestead Winter, lithograph, 1868; Library of Congress

caption: The earliest known engraving of the hill, published in 1841 as "Mormon Hill," a northern view from the road about three miles south of Palmyra.
credit: John W. Barber and Henry Howe, Historical Collections of the State of New York, 1841

file: The Book of Mormon- An Account Written by the Hand of Mormon upon Plates Taken from the Plates of Nephi.jpg
caption: Title page of the first edition of the Book of Mormon, printed by E. B. Grandin in Palmyra, 1830.
credit: The Book of Mormon, first edition (Palmyra: E. B. Grandin, 1830)

caption: A view on the Erie Canal, drawn in 1831, the year Lucy's company traveled the canal west to Buffalo.
credit: John William Hill (1812–1879), View on the Erie Canal, watercolor, 1831; New York Public Library

sec: "Shall We … Build a House for Our God of Logs?"
caption: The Kirtland Temple in an engraving published in 1873, decades after the Saints left Ohio.
credit: Engraving in T. B. H. Stenhouse, The Rocky Mountain Saints, 1873

caption: The Kirtland Temple, photographed in the early twentieth century. Its walls are sandstone rubble under a coat of stucco.
credit: C. R. Savage Co., photograph, published in James E. Talmage, The House of the Lord, 1912

caption: The jail at Liberty in 1888, half in ruins. Andrew Jenson sits on the roof; Edward Stevenson and Joseph S. Black stand beside it.
credit: Photograph, 1888; Church History Library

sec: Before Sunrise on the Mount of Olives
caption: Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, drawn on April 8, 1839, two and a half years before Orson Hyde prayed there.
credit: David Roberts (1796–1864), drawing; Louis Haghe, lithographer, The Holy Land, 1842; Library of Congress

caption: Joseph Smith's red brick store in Nauvoo, photographed in 1885 after it had fallen into disrepair. The Relief Society was organized in its upper room.
credit: Photograph, 1885, attributed to B. H. Roberts

file: The Great Mormon Temple at Nauvoo circa 1848.jpg
caption: "The Great Mormon Temple at Nauvoo," a lithograph of about 1848.
credit: Lithograph, artist unknown, about 1848; Yale Collection of Western Americana, Beinecke Library

caption: The jail at Carthage, engraved for a French travel magazine in 1862.

caption: Gilsum, New Hampshire, where Solomon Mack spent the winter of 1810–11, in a bird’s-eye view of about 1908.
credit: Bird's-eye view of Gilsum, N.H., photographer unknown, about 1908

caption: Main Street in Marlow, New Hampshire, photographed in 1907. Solomon and Lydia Mack moved to Marlow in 1761.
credit: Photographer unknown, 1907

file: South Tunbridge Methodist Episcopal Church, Tunbridge VT.jpg

credit: Photo: John Phelan, 2014

file: Nathan Smith by Ulysses Dow Tenney.jpg

credit: The Holy Bible (London: Robert Barker, 1611), title page

caption: “Farm and Fireside,” an 1878 lithograph of a family evening at home. It is not the Smith family.

caption: Emma Smith in later life, about 1870.
credit: Photographer unknown, about 1870; Brigham Young University

credit: Artist unknown, 19th century
